intended_object: The submodule of invariants V^G = {v ∈ V | ρ(g)v = v for all g ∈ G} of a representation ρ of a monoid G on an R-module V. This comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The carrier is {v | ∀ g, ρ g v = v}, which is exactly the standard fixed-point (invariant) subspace. The closure proofs only use that each ρ g is R-linear. The setting is a semiring R, a monoid G and an additive commutative monoid V. That is the most general setting in which `Representation` is defined in Mathlib, so the definition is not too narrow. Mathlib's own `Representation.invariants` (RepresentationTheory/Invariants.lean) has the same carrier, but it assumes more: `CommRing k`, `Group G` and `AddCommGroup V`. So this definition is a correct generalization of it. There are no problems in degenerate cases: for the trivial monoid it gives all of V, and 0 is always fixed.
